lessons.title: Baby Bo Talks
lessons.targetSound: Consonant and Vowel Slide: ma, ba, se, de, ti, li, bo, ro, fu, gu

storyLines.sentence: Baby Bo sat up in his crib and said, "Ma ma ma!"
"Ba ba ba," he said, and he waved his hands.
Mama giggled and said, "Bo, say se se se."
Bo said, "De de de," and Mama clapped.
"Ti ti ti, li li li," sang Bo as he kicked his feet.
His big sister Ro ran in to hear the new sounds.
"Bo bo bo, ro ro ro!" said Bo, pointing at Ro.
Ro laughed and said, "Fu fu fu, gu gu gu!"
Bo copied her at once: "Fu fu, gu gu!"
Mama slid each sound together: ma, ba, se, de, ti, li.
Then Bo slid bo, ro, fu, and gu without a stop.
Mama and Ro cheered for Baby Bo, the best talker in the house.

questions.question: What is the baby's name?
Who ran in to hear the new sounds?
Which sound did Mama ask Bo to say in line 3?
Write the four sounds Bo slid together at the end of the story.

lessons.title: Robo Says the Slides
lessons.targetSound: Consonant and Vowel Slide: ma, ba, se, de, ti, li, bo, ro, fu, gu

storyLines.sentence: Ti and Li built a robot from a box and some old parts.
They named him Robo, because he could roll.
Robo could not talk, but he could say sounds.
"Ma," said Robo, and he began to march.
"Ba," said Robo, and he began to bounce.
"Se," said Robo, and he sat down in a seat.
"De," said Robo, and he began to dance.
"Ti ti ti, li li li," said Robo, and he tapped his toes.
"Bo," said Robo, and he took a bow.
"Ro," said Robo, and he rolled across the mat.
"Fu, gu!" said Robo, and he did a funny flip.
Ti and Li clapped and said, "Robo, you are the best robot in the world!"

storyLines.sentence: Ben sat in a hut with a bag of hot buns.
A fat bug hid in the bag, but Ben did not see him.
"Yes, I bet this bun is the best," said Ben.
He set a bun on his lap and had a nip.
Just then, the bag gave a hop and a jig.
Ben got up fast and let out a yell.
"Get out, bug!" he said, and he gave the bag a tap.
Out hopped the fat bug, and he sat on the mat.
The bug did not bite, and he did not run.
He just sat with a tiny nod, as if to beg for a bun.
Ben had to grin, and he set a bit of bun by the bug.
"Yes, you can stay, Bud," said Ben, "if you do not rob my bag!"

Jed put in a lot of suds and gave Tug a rub.
Tug let out a yip and a big wag.
Mud and suds hit Jed, and Mom, and the mat!
"Sit, Tug!" said Jed, and Tug sat, wet and glad.
Mom gave a nod and got a mop.
"Yes, Tug is a good pup," said Jed, "but he is a wet, wet pup!"

lessons.title: Tim's Magic Cape
lessons.targetSound: Long and Short Vowels

storyLines.sentence: Tim had a red cape, and it was not just any cape.
When he tapped a cap with it, the cap became a cape.
He tapped a kit, and a kite went up in the sky.
He tapped a pin, and a pine grew tall by his hut.
He tapped a cub, and a cube of ice sat on the mat.
He tapped a plan, and a plane zoomed past his head.
He tapped a tub, and a long, thin tube rolled away.
"Go, go, go!" said Tim, and he clapped his hands with joy.
His cat Mo hid in a box, for she did not want to be tapped.
"No, no," said Tim, "I will not tap you, Mo."
He put the cape in the box, and Mo curled up on top of it.
So the cape stayed a cape, and Mo stayed a cat.

lessons.title: The Note on the Kite

storyLines.sentence: Nat had a kit, and Kate had a kite.
"Let's use tape to fix the tail," said Nat, and he gave it a tap.
Kate wrote a note and tied it to the kite: "Hope you like this kite!"
She did not plan to send it far, but the wind was strong.
Up went the kite, and Kate could not hold on.
It flew past a pine tree, a lake, and a cute cub on a rock.
The cub gave a hop and caught the string in his paws.
Nat and Kate ran up the hill, but they made no sound, for they did not want to scare him.
The cub sat and sniffed the note as if he could read it.
"He can keep it," said Kate. "I made it for a friend, and now I have a cute one!"
Nat gave a nod, and the cub gave a big yawn.
So Nat kept his kit, Kate kept her note, and the cub kept the kite.

Splash! The twins swam fast past the plants and the sticks.
Flip took the lead, but Fran began to sprint ahead through the slippery weeds.
A snake slid by, and a crab snapped, but the twins did not stop.
At the finish, a grand flag flew, and both frogs slapped it at once.
"A tie!" cried Coach Brim, and the crowd clapped and cheered.
The twins crawled onto a flat stone and grinned, glad to have swum their best.

storyLines.sentence: Bill and Hank spent a week at Camp Bluebell, a happy camp by a lake.

"It's the ring!" said Bill, and he gave Hank a wink.
Bill began to sing a song, and the gull tilted its head to listen.
Hank rolled a ball of bread across the grass, and the gull swooped down to grab it.
The ring fell to the ground with a soft ping.
Miss Bell gave both boys a hug, and they sang songs by the campfire all night.

storyLines.sentence: King Ming lived in a tall castle on a hill.

"Thank you, Bill!" said the king. "I think that pup just wanted a song."
The king let the pup keep the bell, and he sang a new song called "Ding, Dong, Pup."
Now the pup rings the bell each day at ten, and the king sings along.

Three judges read the chart and praised every phrase.
Chris felt a thrill from his head to his toes.
The judges gave the shrewd team the first prize.
"A good schedule wins the day!" said Chris with a shrug.

storyLines.sentence: Every year, Yara's family held a party in the yard, and this day was sunny and dry.
Her baby brother was happy and gave a yell of "Yes!" at every game.
Her puppy, Sunny, ran by, yapping at a yellow kite in the sky.
"Why do you want to fly, Sunny?" asked Yara with a giggle.
Uncle Ty told a myth about a boy who tried to fly to the sky.
"Did he try again?" asked Yara. "Yes, he did," said Ty, "and he was not shy about it."
Just then, the baby began to cry, for his candy was gone.
"Do not cry," said Yara. "I will try to find it."
She checked the yard, the fence, and the shady tree.
There sat Sunny with a sticky face and a very funny grin.
Everyone laughed at the silly puppy.
It was a happy day for the whole family, a year to remember.

lessons.title: The Bunny Who Wanted to Fly
lessons.targetSound: Many Jobs of Y

storyLines.sentence: A young bunny named Sunny lived in a yard behind a yellow house.
Every day, he tried to hop as high as the sky.
"Why can't I fly?" he asked a butterfly.
"Bunnies do not fly," said the butterfly, "but you can hop!"
"Yes," said Sunny, "but it is a mystery to me how you fly so high."
The butterfly gave a giggle. "Let's try a trick," she said.
She sat on his ears and flapped, and Sunny hopped as hard as he could.
Up he went, high above the fence, and he saw the whole yard, the road, and the city.
"Wow! I am flying!" he cried with joy.
Down he came, landing on the grass, dizzy and happy.
"Yes, that was my best hop in a year," said Sunny.
The butterfly smiled. "You did fly, just a little."

lessons.title: Gym Day
lessons.targetSound: Many Jobs of Y

storyLines.sentence: Kyle was happy, for it was gym day at school.
Yesterday, his class had practiced jumping, but today they would try yoga.
"Yoga is silly," said Kyle. "My arms will get all twisty."
Ms. Ruby, the gym teacher, said, "Give it a try, Kyle. You might be lucky."
She showed the class a pose called the tree, standing on one leg with the arms held high.
Kyle wobbled and wobbled by a tall bench, and he began to sway.
"Do not cry," said Ms. Ruby. "Try again, and stare at one spot on the wall."
He tried again, and this time he stayed up for a long time.
"Yes!" he yelled. "I can do it!"
His friends clapped, and Kyle gave a big, happy smile.
He did the pose all day, even at lunch, and it was a funny sight.
After school, he told his family, "Yoga is my best thing in gym!"
